sources.entry: simdjson - Where that technique ships, with a kernel per ISA and the harness that keeps its published comparisons reproducible.

summary.one_liner: simdjson is a C++ library that parses JSON (and validates UTF-8, minifies JSON, and handles NDJSON) using SIMD instructions, selecting a CPU-specific parser at runtime.
summary.what_it_does: The library parses JSON using commonly available SIMD instructions and microparallel algorithms, with full JSON and UTF-8 validation and lossless parsing. Its default front-end is the On-Demand API, which the README describes as its main interface, and it is documented as a single .h and .cpp file that can be pulled into a project. It picks a CPU-tailored parser at runtime without configuration. The README also names separate features for minifying JSON, validating UTF-8, and parsing NDJSON, with a multithreaded function for NDJSON files. It includes a number serializer based on the bundled Dragonbox algorithm. The README lists many bindings and language ports (for example Rust, C#, Python, Go, Zig, Java) and cites peer-reviewed papers describing the design.
use_cases: Parse large JSON files quickly in C++
Validate JSON and UTF-8 input at high throughput
Use fast JSON parsing from Python, Rust, C#, Go, or other languages via bindings
how_to_run: Download simdjson.h and simdjson.cpp into a directory (the README uses wget; the URL is not shown in the provided text)
Create quickstart.cpp that includes simdjson.h and uses ondemand::parser
Compile with g++ 7+ or clang++ 6+ (use -std=c++17 with clang++ if needed)
Run the resulting binary against a JSON file such as twitter.json
notable: On-Demand front-end as the default parsing API
Runtime selection of a CPU-tailored parser
Full JSON and UTF-8 validation with lossless parsing
Many bindings and ports across languages, distinguished in the README from full ports
caveats: Requires a 64-bit system with a command-line shell per the Quick Start; other environments such as Visual Studio and Xcode need different steps
README advises product users to work from a tagged release
Performance claims (e.g., GB/s figures) are the project's own; the README does not describe the measurement harness in detail in the provided text
